newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia to import $170 of Russian natgas - paper.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia to import $170 of Russian natgas - paper.

text.p: Yugoslavia plans to import $170 million worth of natural gas from Russia this year in exchange for mostly industrial goods, Belgrade papers reported on Monday.
"The import of natural gas from Russia is within a gas barter deal," papers quoted Toplica Nedeljkovic, director of mixed Russian-Yugoslav company Progresgas Trading.
He said the barter envisaged Yugoslav imports of up to $300 million worth of Russian natural gas a year.

"Yugoslavia has enough goods to pay for the Russian gas," Nedeljkovic said. "In addition to machinery, metal and pharmaceutical products and furniture, Yugoslavia will soon deliver maize, lard, meat and meat products, fruit, vegetables and cooking oil in exchange for gas."
He said the barter arrangement "is one of the best ways for securing a long-term presence of Yugoslav goods on the Russian market and stimulating the growth of industrial production here."
The Petrol Industry of Serbia expects natural gas consumption in the country to reach 4.5 billion cubic metres by the year 2000, papers said.
Yugoslavia, comprising Serbia and Montenegro, made similar barter deal with China on imports of two million tonnes of crude in exchange for domestic products.
